clue.text: Datebook?

parts.note: the clue asks for something that is both a calendar date and a book title: Orwell's dystopian novel named for a year

explanation.walkthrough: 'Datebook' looks like a diary; read it as 'date' plus 'book', a year that is also the title of a famous novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's novel is titled with a year, so the title is at once a date and a book.

clue.text: Party official, one in US government shortly before Trump's termination

indicators.note: in means the number one sits inside the short form for the US government

parts.note: WH is short for the White House, the seat of US government

indicators.note: termination means the final letter of the name

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A party official was one in the US government just before Trump was ousted.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's enforcer in parliament or Congress who keeps members voting along party lines.

clue.text: Try again in seat occupied by male

indicators.note: occupied by means the seat word has the male word sitting inside it

parts.note: rear is a jokey word for one's seat or bottom
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A man sits down in a chair to try a case once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Try' is legal: to hear a case in court again.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that hears a case a second time tries it again.

clue.text: Result of exchanging letters from an Indian city before 1st of March

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: 1st of means the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A trade of letters from an Indian city before the start of March.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchanging letters' sounds like correspondence but means rearranging the letters of a word.
explanation.definitionFit: A word formed by rearranging another's letters is the outcome of such a shuffle, the commonest crossword device.

clue.text: Sweater I reknit, so to speak

indicators.note: to reknit is to knit again in a new pattern, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone says they reknitted a jumper, in a manner of speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are fillers admitting a word is used loosely or figuratively.

clue.text: Dissolute scholar, learner I punish at college

parts.note: prof, short for professor, is a scholar
L is the learner sign on cars in Britain
at Oxford and Cambridge, to gate a student is to confine them to college as punishment

explanation.surface: A debauched academic says: I punish a student at college.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone recklessly given to vice and wasteful indulgence.

clue.text: Soul of an MP disturbed about what UK's abandoning

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go round the union's letters
disturbed means upset or thrown into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the UK left the European Union at the end of January 2020

explanation.surface: A troubled MP's soul over Brexit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbed' rearranges AN MP into PNMA, and 'about' puts it round EU.
explanation.definitionFit: In theology and Greek philosophy the word names the spirit or breath of life.

clue.text: Date of historic score, with combinations of sixes

definitions.meaning: Tchaikovsky's overture is named for the year Napoleon retreated from Moscow
three sixes added together and two sixes added together give the two numbers

explanation.surface: A historic match result is dated by tallying sixes, as in a cricket innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' suggests a sports result, but here it is a piece of music: Tchaikovsky's overture. Eighteen is 6+6+6 and twelve is 6+6.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous overture by Tchaikovsky bears the year of the 1812 campaign as its title; the numbers are also sums of sixes.

clue.text: 10, or part of 24 down

definitions.meaning: the answer to 10 across, meaning a jump
one of the four seasons of the answer to 24 down

explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a jump, synonym of the first half of the themed phrase; the other is a season, one part of a twelvemonth.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring is to jump, and spring is also a season, one quarter of a calendar twelvemonth.

clue.text: English novel a player pens, for example 1 11

indicators.note: pens means encloses, so the words a player hold the letter for English
novel means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An English novel in which a performer writes, offered as an example of a famous book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book, especially beside 'English' and the Orwell cross-reference, but it is the anagram signal. A PLAYER is rearranged to LEAPYAR, which 'pens' E.
explanation.definitionFit: 1984 had a twenty-ninth of February, so it is one instance of a year with an extra day.

clue.text: See 1 down
Proverbial loser in 10 24 down regularly scrapped with partners initially

indicators.note: initially means the partners' letters come first, ahead of the rest

parts.note: W and E, West and East, are partners at the bridge table

indicators.note: regularly scrapped means every other letter of the cross-referenced phrase is thrown away

parts.note: the answer to 10 across and 24 down, a year with an extra day

explanation.surface: In a year with an extra day, the proverbial loser was routinely thrown out along with his partners.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'finders keepers, losers weepers'. 'Partners' are a bridge pair, and 'regularly scrapped' throws away the odd letters of the cross-referenced phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: In the playground rhyme 'finders keepers, losers weepers', the one who loses something is the one who cries.

clue.text: It's contested quadrennially, bringing power and official place to live

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
a residency is an official residence, such as an ambassador's

explanation.surface: A four-yearly contest brings power and an official home.
explanation.walkthrough: US presidential elections fall every four years, in leap years.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of US head of state is fought over in an election held every four years.

clue.text: Issue of Trump, in part, dividing a piece of the US

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the other words apart by sitting in their middle

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
Eric Trump is one of Donald Trump's children, so one part of his issue

explanation.surface: A dispute over Trump splits a region of the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' sounds like a political question but means offspring. Eric Trump goes inside A MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything belonging to or coming from the United States.

clue.text: Like promise broken, broken by male like Boris

indicators.note: broken by means split open with another letter pushed inside

parts.note: a promise that has been broken is one not kept

explanation.surface: A broken promise, broken again by a man like Boris Johnson.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Johnson, then UK Prime Minister, was known for his tousled hair; 'like promise broken' also hints at his reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Johnson's famously untidy mop of hair makes a scruffy, uncombed look his trademark.

clue.text: Romantic female role today for model

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a poser is someone who poses, like a model

explanation.surface: A romantic woman's part today, for an artist's model.
explanation.walkthrough: By tradition a woman may propose marriage on 29 February, the day the puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: On leap day, by custom, the woman asks for a hand in marriage, taking the asking role.

clue.text: Member of jury in recent trial — treason involved?

definitions.text: Member of jury in recent trial

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Was treason at issue for a juror in a recent high-profile trial?
explanation.walkthrough: The trial is Trump's 2020 impeachment, in which the Senate sits as jury.
explanation.definitionFit: In a US impeachment trial the upper house acts as the jury, so each of its members is a juror.

clue.text: Dweller on mountain, one seeking gold in 10 24 down

definitions.meaning: the Greek gods lived on Mount Olympus
a competitor in the Games, which are usually held in years with an extra day

explanation.surface: A mountain-dweller hunting gold in a leap year.
explanation.definitionFit: A Greek god living on Mount Olympus, and also an athlete competing at the summer Games for a medal.

clue.text: Impeach, as a restraint, in hearing

indicators.note: in hearing means as heard spoken, so the words are a soundalike

parts.note: the indefinite article, A; a rein is a strap that restrains a horse

explanation.surface: Impeachment as a restraint, during a hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hearing' looks like a court session in the impeachment surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge someone formally with an offence, as an impeachment does.

clue.text: Iron hook smashed large stone

indicators.note: smashed means broken into pieces, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An iron hook was smashed by a big rock.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koh-i-Noor is one of the largest cut diamonds in the world, part of the British Crown Jewels.

clue.text: Difference between 2020 and 2019, at some point

definitions.meaning: 2020 has 366 days and 2019 has 365, so the gap is a single twenty-four hours
an indefinite future time, as in 'we will meet some time'

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what separates two years, settled eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: A leap year exceeds a common year by a single twenty-four-hour span, and the phrase also means sometime.

clue.text: Even you, in old-fashioned way, decorate fabric

parts.note: a game ending even is a tied game
ye is an archaic form of you

explanation.surface: Even you could colour cloth the traditional way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tie-dyeing is a technique of colouring cloth by knotting it before dipping it in dye.

clue.text: See 8
Left author to judge paper again, for instance

parts.note: red is the colour of the political left
Umberto Eco was an Italian author
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: A left-wing writer is asked to assess a newspaper a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' is a verb here: to wallpaper a room again is one way to do it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Putting up fresh wallpaper is one example of doing up a room afresh.

clue.text: Setter might produce them, ending off this month with a little extra added

indicators.note: ending off means take only the final letter of the month's name

parts.note: the puzzle appeared at the end of February 2020
PS, a postscript, is a little extra added to a letter

explanation.surface: The setter has produced this puzzle at the close of the month with a bit extra, the leap day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' seems to be the crossword's compiler but is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A setter is a breed of dog, and short sharp barks are what such a dog lets out.

clue.text: See 10
Inexperienced cowboy cut end of rope

indicators.note: cut means trimmed, so the cowboy word loses its final letter

parts.note: a gaucho is a South American cowboy

indicators.note: end of means take the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A green cowhand cuts the end off his rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and lacking social polish, the word is a loose synonym for green or naive.

clue.text: Eg clue that's really simple and good? Brendan's not without method

parts.note: Brendan, the setter, says of himself I've a way: he is not lacking a method

explanation.surface: A setter boasts that even his easy clues have method behind them.
explanation.walkthrough: Brendan is this puzzle's setter, so 'Brendan's' stands for 'I've', and 'not without method' gives 'a way'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue so easy it reveals its own answer is said to be a freebie that hands the solution over.
